content: [{"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Infrastructure", "col": 12}, "id": "b0"}, {"type": "chart", "data": {"chart_name": "File Scans by Verdict", "col": 12}, "id": "b1"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The platform services the CRM runs on \u2014 file storage, screening, maps, search and list computation \u2014 are configured here.", "col": 12}, "id": "b2"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Configured here", "col": 12}, "id": "b3"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Blob storage and screening rules decide where an attachment lands and whether it is admitted. Search aliases and derived fields shape what a list can find and show.", "col": 12}, "id": "b4"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Watched here", "col": 12}, "id": "b5"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "File scan log records each screening verdict and the action taken.", "col": 12}, "id": "b6"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Documentation server (MCP)", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp1"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An AI assistant belonging to a member of staff can be pointed at this site to read the handbook, the live field definitions and the Desk map, and talk that person through a task in the CRM's own words. It is read-only: it returns no lead, task, call or patient, and it changes nothing. Every read is served by the read replica, so it never touches the database the CRM writes to.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp2"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Switch it on. The server is dormant until MCP::Docs::server is enabled in Engine Switches. While it is off every call is answered \u201cnot enabled\u201d and no query runs.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp3"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Set the limits. Open MCP Settings below. Two counters guard the site: one per person, so a runaway assistant cannot starve anyone else, and one shared by everyone, which is the ceiling that protects the site itself. The answer sizes below them bound what a single call costs to build and to read.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp4"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Issue a key. Access is a normal Frappe API key on a normal user, issued here by an administrator \u2014 staff do not generate their own. Open the user in Users, generate the key and secret, and hand both to that person once; the secret is shown only at that moment. The server answers as that user, so what they may read is decided by their own roles and nothing else.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp5"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Hand over the address. The person adds https://one.tatvacare.in/mcp in their AI tool, with the header Authorization: token <key>:<secret>. Nothing else is configured on their side. Revoking access is deleting the key, or disabling the user.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp6"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Watched here. Every call is logged like any other external request \u2014 who called, which tool, how long it took \u2014 under channel MCP in the API request log.", "col": 12}, "id": "mcp7"}, {"type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}, "id": "mcp8"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "MCP Settings", "col": 4}, "id": "mcp9"}, {"type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}, "id": "b7"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Azure Storage", "col": 4}, "id": "b8"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Screening", "col": 4}, "id": "b9"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Maps", "col": 4}, "id": "b10"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Search Aliases", "col": 4}, "id": "b11"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Derived Fields", "col": 4}, "id": "b12"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Log Settings", "col": 4}, "id": "b13"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Files", "col": 4}, "id": "b14"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Scan Log", "col": 4}, "id": "b15"}]
